paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from Daniel. His enemies went looking for a charge against him and found NOTHING, because he was trustworthy (Daniel 6:4). They said they would never find one "unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God" (Daniel 6:5), and I think that's the biggest compliment a baker could ever get.

Then the decree gets signed, and Daniel does what he always does. He kneels three times a day, prays and gives thanks to his God, "just as he had done before" (Daniel 6:10). Nobody could change the king's law, but Daniel's habit stayed right where it was. Friend, the daily stuff you do when nobody's pushing you is what holds up when the pressure comes.

In the morning, the king cries out, "has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?" (Daniel 6:20). Daniel's answer is that his God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions (Daniel 6:22), and no wounds were found on him, "because he had trusted in his God" (Daniel 6:23). Even King Darius ends up writing that God "delivers and rescues," and that His kingdom "will never be destroyed" (Daniel 6:26, 27). So keep trusting Him, baker, because the God who rescued Daniel is the same God who will never stop being the living God.
